item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Fresh Yemen clashes kill more than 60, including 26 soldiers
item.description:
Fresh Yemen clashes kill more than 60, including 26 soldiers

Fighting between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the country's Houthi rebels killed more than 60 people on Saturday, including civilians, medical and military sources told AFP.

The renewed clashes in Yemen's southwest over control of a gateway to the Red Sea came after Friday saw some of the deadliest fighting in years, following the collapse in July of a 2022 ceasefire. 

According to three Yemeni military sources, 26 government troops were killed during several hours of fighting in the country's southwest, while medical and military sources from the Iran-backed Houthis said 31 rebel fighters were killed. 

One medical source in the government-held city of Taiz said a missile strike also killed six civilians travelling by bus and wounded seven others. 

A government official blamed the strike on the bus, travelling between Taiz and the seat of Yemen's internationally recognised government in Aden, on the Houthis.

In Taiz, a military officer said the "coming hours will be decisive" after the Houthis seized positions near the city a day earlier.

The officer added that reinforcements had been arriving from Aden in response to the Houthi offensive, which aims to cut off the government-held port city of Mokha, under fire for weeks, and advance towards areas bordering the Bab al-Mandab strait.

In Hays district, 68 kilometres northwest of Taiz towards the Red Sea coast, AFP journalists saw government forces being ferried to the front lines in pickup trucks, some carrying assault rifles and others with rocket-propelled grenades slung over their shoulders.

Rashed Maghari, a Hays resident, said "there has been heavy Houthi shelling on Hays and its residents, but the district is tough" and will be hard to capture.

On Friday, the fighting in Yemen killed 129 people, according to an AFP tally compiled from several sources. 

(Report by AFP)

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Netanyahu dismisses 'all this controversy' around Qatar as 'big hoax'
item.description:
Netanyahu dismisses 'all this controversy' around Qatar as 'big hoax'

Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu has dismissed “all this controversy around Qatar” as a “big hoax”.

In an interview with Israel’s i24NEWS, he said: "I attacked Qatar, and not only that, I bombed it and launched attacks on it during the war, and in turn, it attacked me.”  

“All this controversy around Qatar is nothing but a big hoax. Qatar is a hostile state, but it has not imposed its conditions or will on us here in any way whatsoever."  

Netanyahu was apparently referring to former prime minister Naftali Bennett’s repeated assertions that Israel was not doing enough to declare Qatar as an enemy state.

Bennett, who is president of the Together party, has promised to classify Qatar among the enemy states of Israel if he returned to power, accusing Doha of "setting up a vast international influence operation aimed at weakening Israel".

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Gaza death toll since October 2023 rises to 73,651, health ministry says
item.description:
Gaza death toll since October 2023 rises to 73,651, health ministry says

Israel has killed 73,651 Palestinians and injured 174,575 others as of 5 September 2026, since launching what rights groups and UN officials have described as a genocidal military campaign on Gaza following Hamas's attacks on 7 October 2023, according to the territory's health ministry.

Wafa news agency reported that hospitals in Gaza received 17 bodies over the past 48 hours, including five newly killed people, one who succumbed to injuries, and 11 bodies recovered from under the rubble, in addition to 27 injured Palestinians.

They added that the number of Palestinians killed since the ceasefire took effect on 11 October 2025, has risen to 1,344, while 4,464 others have been injured. A total of 815 bodies have also been recovered.

Wafa said that 160 additional Palestinian fatalities were added to the cumulative death toll after their records were completed and verified during August.

According to Wafa, health officials said a number of victims remain trapped beneath rubble and on roads, with rescue and ambulance crews struggling to reach them.

item.description:
Middle East crude oil exports in August down 39 percent, TankerTrackers says

Crude oil exports out of the Middle East during August 2026 were down 39 percent since the January and February baseline of 18.5 million barrels per day (mbpd), according to oil-tracking firm TankerTrackers.

The sharpest fall of 67 percent below pre-war levels was recorded in May, the firm said, adding that the current deficit is now only 7.2 mbpd, compared with 12.4 mbpd in May.

The firm covered Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Iran, Kuwait, Oman, the UAE and Qatar in its assessment.

Gaza holds funeral for 100 Palestinians recovered from rubble

A funeral was held in Gaza on Saturday for around 100 Palestinians whose bodies were recovered from the rubble of homes destroyed in Israeli attacks, Reuters reported.

The ceremony took place in the Zeitoun neighbourhood, southeast of Gaza City, where relatives and residents gathered to mourn the victims.

According to Gaza civil defence authorities, the deceased included 55 members of the Malka family, whose remains were recovered underneath the rubble of a building in the Zeytoun area.

The victims had sought refuge in the building roughly two years ago during an Israeli bombing campaign.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Kites flown across 11 Dutch cities in solidarity with Gaza children
item.description:
Kites flown across 11 Dutch cities in solidarity with Gaza children

Kites were flown across 11 cities in the Netherlands on Saturday in solidarity with children in Gaza.

The events, organised by the Plant an Olive Tree Foundation, sought to draw attention to attacks on Gaza and protest Israeli threats of displacement and attacks against Palestinians over kites flown from the enclave that landed in Israeli settlements near the border.

In Rotterdam, participants gathered at Noordereiland Square and flew kites in solidarity with children in Gaza.

Children and adults decorated the kites with Palestinian flags and colours, as well as messages including “Free Palestine” and “Save Gaza.”

Kites designed in the shape and colors of the Palestinian flag were also flown during the event.

At the end of the demonstration, participants distributed leaflets to raise public awareness and provide information about the situation in Gaza.

📍Zwolle, Netherlands

Dutch children in Zwolle flew vibrant kites adorned with the Palestinian flag, sending a message of love and support to the children of Gaza.🪁🇵🇸 pic.twitter.com/lXaDNbl6SC

Taraneh and Romina Rahimi had been seized over their decision to join millions on the streets of Iranian cities during the January protests against the regime. The twins were unrecognisable by the time of their mother’s prison visit in May.
